body:
Motivation
Fixes #33187.
SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS maps NaN logits to -1e30, which stops the sampling kernels from returning out-of-vocab ids. But for a row that is entirely NaN it also produces a constant row — a uniform distribution over the vocabulary. Sampling that returns a uniformly random token, which means:
	•	the request streams vocabulary noise to the client as a healthy 200, with no error signal anywhere;
	•	EOS probability collapses to ~1/vocab_size per step, so the request does not terminate normally;
	•	the corrupted KV is inserted into the radix tree and can reach unrelated requests through prefix matching.
Sanitization remains the right call for a partial NaN row — the surviving logits still carry real evidence about the next token. The full-row case is the one with no safe recovery.
Modifications
New SGLANG_ABORT_ON_NAN_LOGITS (default off), a third mode with a request-scoped blast radius alongside the existing crash and sanitize behaviors:
	•	Detect (utils/async_probe.py, layers/sampler.py) — detect_full_nan_rows returns a [#seq] bool mask, read in Sampler.forward on the raw model output before _preprocess_logits sanitizes it away. Returns None (zero work) when the env is off.
	•	Carry (layers/logits_processor.py, managers/utils.py) — the mask travels on LogitsProcessorOutput, and its D2H is appended to copy_to_cpu so it rides the existing next_token_ids copy and its copy_done event. No new synchronization.
	•	Abort (managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py) — _abort_full_nan_logits_reqs runs in both the prefill and decode result paths, before update_finish_state consumes req.to_finish. Each flagged request gets FINISH_ABORT(..., HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE) — the same mechanism and status as the existing running-timeout abort, which TokenizerManager._handle_abort_finish_reason already turns into a retriable 503 for both streaming and non-streaming clients.
	•	Cache hygiene — flagged requests also set skip_radix_cache_insert, the existing Req flag meaning “this request’s KV must never be shared” (until now set only for the PD-disaggregation fake-bootstrap case). release_kv_cache then frees the KV without publishing it to the radix tree, and maybe_cache_unfinished_req skips it too, so prefix matching cannot spread the corruption.
	•	Partial-row NaN is unchanged — those rows still carry real evidence about the next token, so they fall through to sanitization.
Supporting changes:
	•	Throttled logging — _AsyncNanWarner latched on the first hit and went silent for the process lifetime, hiding whether a NaN burst was ongoing. It now counts events and warns at most once per interval, reporting how many forward passes each line covers. Detection stays sync-free (device counter → pinned host memory).
	•	Two defensive getattrs dropped — mem_cache/common.py read skip_radix_cache_insert through getattr(req, ..., False) in both maybe_cache_unfinished_req and release_kv_cache. The attribute is assigned unconditionally in Req.__init__, so neither guard was ever needed.
Scope note: the mask is produced by Sampler.forward only, which is reached from ModelRunner.sample — one logits row per request, so it indexes batch.reqs directly (asserted). Speculative workers verify through their own sampling path in speculative/eagle_utils.py and leave the mask unset, so spec decoding keeps today’s sanitize-only behavior. The reporter in #33187 ran with speculative decoding disabled. Extending coverage to the verify path needs stride-aware row→request mapping and is left for a follow-up.
Known limitation: on the prefill/decode path the sampled token is appended to output_ids before update_finish_state consumes the abort, so a streaming client may see one final noise token alongside the abort finish reason. Non-streaming clients get the 503 and no text. Suppressing that token would mean branching in the per-request hot loop; happy to add it if reviewers prefer.
Accuracy Tests
Not applicable. Model outputs change only in the failure case this targets — a request that would have emitted uniformly random tokens now returns 503 instead — and only when the new env var is explicitly enabled. The default leaves existing behavior unchanged.
New unit tests (test/registered/unit/utils/test_abort_on_nan_logits.py, CPU, base-a-test-cpu), run locally against the current branch:

Ran 7 tests in 0.004s

OK


They cover full-vs-partial row detection, the env-off no-op, the sanitize→uniform mechanism the fix exists to prevent, the abort’s status code and cache-insert coupling, the finished/retracted skip, and the one-row-per-request assertion. test_module_state_ratchet and test_legacy_global_ratchet were also re-run and pass.
Speed Tests and Profiling
No steady-state cost when SGLANG_ABORT_ON_NAN_LOGITS is off: detect_full_nan_rows returns None before touching the tensor, and the D2H is skipped. When on, it adds one isnan().all(-1) reduction per sampling step and a [#seq] bool D2H that rides the existing copy event.
The throttled-logging change does add work under SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS: the previous latch stopped the per-step isnan().any() reduction after the first warning, and it now runs every step. That reduction is over the same tensor nan_to_num_ already scans unconditionally on that path, so it is one extra pass on an opt-in debug path.
Checklist
	•	Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. — isort, black, and ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037 all clean over the changed files.
	•	Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. — 7 new CPU tests, passing (see Accuracy Tests).
	•	Update documentation according to Write documentations. — added the SGLANG_ABORT_ON_NAN_LOGITS row to environment_variables.mdx, and corrected the adjacent SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS default, which the table listed as true while environ.py has EnvBool(False).
	•	Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to Test the accuracy and Benchmark the speed. — not applicable, see above.
	•	Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
Review and Merge Process
	1.	Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the PR Merge Process.
	2.	Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers.
	3.	Trigger CI tests with comments or contact authorized users to do so.
	•	Common commands include /tag-and-rerun-ci, /tag-run-ci-label, /rerun-failed-ci
	4.	After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
